finding_en: Randomised double-blind trial in 144 women after caesarean section: a topical Hypericum perforatum ointment was associated with better wound-healing scores on day 10 and less scarring on day 40 than a placebo ointment or no ointment.
Laboratory study of 29 isolates of common burn-wound pathogens: dilute acetic acid (0.16-0.31 percent) inhibited growth, prevented biofilm formation and eradicated mature biofilms after three hours.
note: Laboratory data only; acetic acid, not vinegar.

finding_en: Narrative review of acetic acid as a topical agent for Pseudomonas aeruginosa wound infections, including multidrug-resistant strains.
note: Narrative review; acetic acid, not vinegar.

finding_en: Cochrane review of 26 trials (3011 participants): honey appeared to heal partial-thickness burns more quickly than conventional dressings; the authors rate most of the evidence as low quality.
note: Moderate-quality evidence for partial-thickness burns only.

finding_en: Same Cochrane review: for minor acute wounds, venous leg ulcers, diabetic foot ulcers and mixed chronic wounds the effect of honey was unclear (low or very low quality evidence).
